skill.name: verification-hygiene
skill.description: Guides external evidence verification by classifying claims, routing searches, tiering sources, checking independence, and formatting findings before final reasoning.
skill.summary: Routes verification work through disciplined search, source tiering, and evidence formatting.
skill.author: SyntagmaNull

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick and system reconnaissance findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fact-checking examples. One semantic concern remains: the skill claims controlled-trial approval without verifiable marketplace attestation. No executable code, shell commands, network endpoints, or data exfiltration instructions were found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Unverified approval claim in the skill status section.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the approval claim or replace it with neutral lifecycle metadata verified outside the skill text.

content.user_title: Verify External Evidence with Source Discipline
content.value_statement: Unstructured web search can turn stale or repeated claims into false confidence. This skill routes verification through target types, source tiers, freshness checks, and abstention rules.
actual_capabilities: Classifies verification targets as events, status checks, sources, media context, policies, metrics, or evaluation records.
Builds neutral, disconfirming, and provenance search strategies for external evidence checks.
Ranks evidence by primary, credible secondary, and tertiary source tiers.
Checks whether multiple sources are independent or repeat one origin.
Formats evidence with claim comparison, temporal status, source basis, and conflict notes.
Stops verification when evidence is sufficient or when only low quality sources remain.
limitations: It does not perform searches by itself without the host agent and available tools.
It depends on the model to apply the routing rules consistently.
It cannot prove facts when authoritative sources are unavailable.
The source document states it is not approved for general deployment.

use_cases.title: Check Current Rules
use_cases.description: Verify whether a policy, law, product feature, or platform rule is current before answering.

use_cases.title: Trace Viral Claims
use_cases.description: Find the source, date, and original context for quotes, screenshots, videos, or social claims.

use_cases.title: Reduce Search Bias
use_cases.description: Convert loaded prompts into neutral and disconfirming searches before forming a conclusion.
use_cases.target_user: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Simple Claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Use verification hygiene to check this claim. Identify the target type, choose authoritative sources, and state whether the claim is supported.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use verification hygiene for a status question. Prefer current official sources and mark freshness as current, outdated, or unknown.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Source Provenance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use verification hygiene to trace this claim to its earliest reliable source. Separate origin evidence from repeated commentary.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Conflicting Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use verification hygiene to compare these conflicting sources. Test independence, map disagreements, and decide whether to support, contradict, or abstain.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether a platform policy changed this week.
output_examples.output: The response identifies a status target, uses the latest official policy page, and marks older summaries as secondary context.

output_examples.input: A user repeats a viral quote attributed to a public figure.
output_examples.output: The response traces the quote origin, notes repeated sources, and marks the claim unresolved when no primary record appears.

output_examples.input: A user asks why a company intentionally caused a market event.
output_examples.output: The response removes the loaded premise, searches neutral event facts, and separates evidence from motive claims.

best_practices: Classify the verification target before searching.
Prefer primary sources when the answer depends on current rules, metrics, or official actions.
Use abstention when only tertiary or repeated sources are available.
anti_patterns: Do not copy the user premise into a search query without neutralizing it.
Do not count repeated articles as independent evidence.
Do not turn public sentiment into factual proof.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the web automatically?
faq.answer: No. It tells the host model how to route and evaluate searches when search tools are available.

faq.question: What sources does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers official databases, court records, original media, policy pages, and primary research when those sources fit the claim.

faq.question: How does it handle conflicting sources?
faq.answer: It maps the disagreement, checks whether sources are independent, and lowers confidence when the conflict remains unresolved.

faq.question: Can it answer medical or legal questions?
faq.answer: It can guide evidence checks, but high stakes answers still require current authoritative sources and careful domain review.

faq.question: Why does it use disconfirming searches?
faq.answer: Disconfirming searches reduce confirmation bias and help detect loaded user premises.

faq.question: Is it ready for general deployment?
faq.answer: The source document says it is not approved for general deployment, so teams should review it before production use.
